# Pinocchio Native Marker Forward Kinematics

## Scope

F09e (#11914) extends the F09d native marker-output boundary to the actual
Pinocchio full-state torque replay in F06c (#11900). The replay is executed
once through `replay_native_pinocchio_torque_bundle`; marker positions are
then evaluated from that returned configuration trajectory. This layer does
not integrate dynamics, score observations, or qualify a model.

## Native Frame Mapping

For each replay state, the existing `PinocchioPhysicsEngine` updates its native
frame placements. An ordered attachment names one exact Pinocchio frame and a
local SI point. The output position is

$$
p^w_i = t^w_f(q_i) + R^w_f(q_i) r^f,
$$

where $q_i$ is the configuration emitted by replay, and $r^f$ is the explicit
finite three-vector offset in metres. Marker labels and frame names are unique
and ordered. Unknown or ambiguous frame names, stale source/provider/model
identity, non-finite points, changed input/policy digest, and incomplete q/v
history are rejected.

The F01 row's package, variant and drive mode remain distinct from the native
bundle's `model_id`, native `variant_id`, execution provider, loaded model,
state schema, ordered channels and executed policy. The binding must match both
namespaces exactly. It does not infer a production model mapping from a
synthetic fixture.

## State and Numerical Policy

The complete physical state has Pinocchio configuration `qpos` and tangent
velocity `qvel`. The fixture's free-flyer model has $n_q=8$ and $n_v=7$; these
dimensions are never conflated. Native frame placements are derived caches,
not independently supplied physical state. The native execution policy binds
fresh-engine initialization and forbids state resets. The reset count remains
unknown (`None`); a policy declaration is not a measured zero.

The output preserves the replay's exact simulation-relative time grid and is
content-addressed with its unqualified F09c execution receipt, F09d marker map,
and marker positions. All model/drive inventory rows and six required engines
remain represented. Pinocchio fixture coverage does not turn missing MyoSuite,
OpenSim or Simscape providers into passes; OpenSim's separate F07 geometry
provider is only usable after full-state replay identity is available.

## Verification and Limits

The synthetic Pinocchio 4.1 URDF uses nonzero free-flyer translation and yaw,
nonzero hinge position, a nonzero joint origin, and a nonzero marker-local
offset. Expected world points are composed independently from the analytic
root and hinge transforms and compared with the native `oMf` result. It checks
software identity and transform conventions only. It does not establish
anatomical attachment, contact, muscle behavior, observed-marker accuracy,
production-model support, or cross-engine equivalence.

Focused command:

```text
python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/unit/engines tests/unit/engines/test_feedback_native_markers.py
```

The actual Pinocchio 4.1 case runs in the owned Ubuntu 24.04 environment
`codex-feedback-pinocchio-11900`; the default Windows interpreter may skip it
when the optional provider is absent. The design-manual calculation inventory
remains empty and release remains blocked.
